title: Lumen watchhand briefing - cache latency spike and follow-ups
content:
Shift: Lumen watch (18:00-02:00 UTC)
Owner: Aisha Patel (primary) | Noah Kim (secondary)
Quick summary:
- Short window (~18:42-19:08 UTC) of elevated p50/p95 tail latency for hosted text-generation routes. Root apparent: KV/prefix cache eviction storms on dedicated caches -> read amplification into GPU-serving layer.
- Impact: increased per-request latency, a handful of customer requests hit routing fallback to smaller model variants. No data loss, no auth failures.
- Severity: Sev-2 briefly, auto-escalated to on-call SRE + serving-runtime on-call. Incident tag JIRA-RI-2026-12-27-4 created.

Timeline (high level):
- 18:39 UTC: alert - latency spike on route /v1/generate-hosted (p95 > 750ms threshold for 3m).
- 18:41 UTC: paging SRE on-call (me), paged serving-runtime on-call (Miguel).
- 18:42 UTC: observed large KV cache churn across 3 cache shards in eu-west-1. Cloudwatch/Prometheus graph attached to Jira.
- 18:45 UTC: applied temporary rate-limit on non-prod tenant traffic to reduce pressure (route-level in API gateway).
- 18:49 UTC: shifted some traffic to dedicated fallback pool for affected premium tenant via routing policy override. Reduced p95 to ~320ms.
- 19:02 UTC: safe window; cache hit-rate improved after prefix-cache stabilization and small batch of retained prefixes warmed back in.
- 19:08 UTC: alerts returned to normal.

Actions taken (what we did):
- Immediate: rate-limited noisy non-prod keys (api-key: test-bench-*) at gateway for 20m.
- Temporary routing tweak: forced heavy-profile tenants to fallback model variant with lower KV dependency.
- Investigated metrics: KV cache eviction rate, cache-size-by-shard, allocator GC cycles. Ran quick queries against metrics (prometheus): 
    - prometheus query used: sum(rate(cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)
- Mitigation: adjusted cache eviction threshold on two eu-west-1 shards (+10% size) to reduce immediate churn (config change rolled via infra job).
- Communication: updated #sre-ops slack thread and created incident Jira. Notified Customer Success for any churned customer activity.

Observations and clues for post-incident analysis:
- Eviction storm correlated with a burst of batch-infer jobs from internal load-testing (unlabelled keys) that started at 18:40. Need to trace the source.
- One shard showed slightly elevated OOM events at the process level (killed small helper process) while main inference daemons remained healthy.
- Autoscaler did not spin a new shard because the control-plane policy considered short-lived spikes as noise. Maybe tune the `scale_cooldown` to be slightly shorter for cache layer.
- Serving-runtime logs show increased kv-store read-latency under saturation (tail reads).

Runbook notes / draft changes (actionable edits to add to runbook):
- Add an emergency procedure for "KV eviction storm":
    1) Immediately identify noisy API keys using `redis top-k eviction` equivalent or prometheus label 'api_key'.
    2) Add temporary gateway rate-limit on offending key(s).
    3) Increase shard cache-size by +10-25% for 15m and monitor hit-rate.
    4) If autoscaler doesn't respond within 2m, trigger manual scale-up and mark control-plane policy for review.
    5) If read-latency is > 200ms p95 after 10m, consider routing to fallback model variants per tenant.
- Add a short play to identify internal load tests: correlate with infra job ids (jenkins/gha) using timestamp and user-agent. Quick command hint in runbook: `kubectl logs -l app=launcher -n infra --since=15m | grep loadtest`
- Include runbook snippet to gather artifacts: prometheus queries used, relevant logs commands, which dashboards to snapshot, and a checklist for SSD/IO saturation checks on cache nodes.

Open follow-ups (owners + ETA):
- Investigate origin of the load-testing burst (likely internal): Assign to Miguel Santos. ETA 2026-12-30. Link: JIRA-RI-2026-12-27-4 -> SUBTASK-1.
- Formalize KV eviction runbook section and set tabletop drill: Assign to Grace Huang. ETA draft by 2027-01-07.
- Tune cache autoscaler `scale_cooldown` for cache layer: assign eng-infra (Noah). ETA 2027-01-04.
- Post-incident perf test to validate scaling behavior under synthetic eviction storms: assign eng-serving-runtime. ETA 2027-01-14.

Notes to next shift (short bullets):
- Watch eu-west-1 cache hit-rate for next 24h; I enabled a temporary alert with lower threshold (p95 > 300ms) for 12h.
- If repeated eviction spikes: revert gateway allowlist for heavy tenants and escalate to product for possible quota changes.
- Check SQS backlog for model-fallback queue. There was a small increase at 18:50 but drained by 19:10.
- If you see new OOMs on cache helper processes, gather `dmesg` and attach to Jira.

Quick troubleshooting commands (notes for on-call):
- Cache shard status: `curl -s http://cache-admin.eu-west-1.internal/shards | jq .`
- Prometheus queries (use grafana explore): `sum(rate(cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_store_read_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
- Check autoscaler decisions: `kubectl get hpa -n cache -o yaml` and `kubectl logs deployment/cache-autoscaler -n cache --since=20m`

Communications and customer impact notes:
- Customer Success notified two impacted premium tenants with a short note; no escalations opened.
- Email template drafted in Jira comment for CS to use if customers request detail.

Misc / loose ideas:
- Consider labelled keys for internal load tests so they don't count against customer caches. Small infra change but would reduce noisy neighbor events.
- Evaluate having a small "reserve" cache shard in each region that can be promoted during eviction storms (fast warm).

Appendix: artifacts captured (attached to Jira):
- Grafana snapshots (cache-hit-rate, evictions, cpu/io for cache nodes)
- Serving-runtime logs 18:35-19:15 UTC (filtered)
- A brief heap/pmem snapshot from shard-2 at 18:50 (no smoking gun)

End of shift handoff:
- Next on-call: Noah Kim (starts 02:00 UTC).
- Please poke me if any questions about the temporary gateway changes — I will be around until 21:30 UTC for quick clarifications.

Todo checklist (for next 24h):
- [ ] Confirm source of internal loadtest (Miguel)
- [ ] Draft eviction section in runbook (Grace)
- [ ] Short autoscaler config tweak PR (Noah)
- [ ] Schedule 1-hour post-incident review with eng-serving-runtime and infra (tentative 2027-01-05)

---
Notes to self: keep runbook short and prescriptive. Avoid too many manual steps that depend on human memory.
